issues.observed: Months are displayed in a nonchronological order such as April, August, December, February and January. Connecting these categories with lines produces a false time sequence.
issues.desired: Both trend charts should progress chronologically through the fiscal or calendar year, with the period definition clearly stated.
issues.action: Sort MonthName by a numeric MonthNumber or FiscalMonthNumber column and then sort both visuals ascending. If multiple fiscal years are shown, use a continuous Year-Month field or a correctly ordered fiscal period key.

issues.observed: Revenue and YoY Growth % are plotted as clustered series despite having incompatible units. The percentage marks collapse near zero and are effectively unreadable.
issues.desired: Revenue magnitude and growth rate should both be visible without implying that currency and percentage share one scale.
issues.action: For regional performance, use Power BI's line and clustered column chart with revenue as columns, YoY growth as a line, and a clearly labelled secondary percentage axis. For category performance, use separate aligned revenue bars and growth indicators or another native visual arrangement that preserves distinct scales.

issues.observed: The slicers prominently display individual values such as FY 2022, London and Beauty, but their selection state is ambiguous. At the same time, visuals show multiple years, regions and categories, making it difficult to determine the active scope.
issues.desired: Executives should immediately understand whether the page represents the entire business or a filtered subset.
issues.action: Use compact dropdown slicers with explicit All states, add a Reset filters button, and display an active-filter summary or dynamic subtitle. Validate visual interactions so every intended visual responds consistently to each slicer.

issues.observed: A large green header area is mostly blank and the page has no visible Executive Overview title, reporting period, refresh date or concise business context.
issues.desired: The top of the page should establish page purpose, reporting period and current filter context before presenting KPIs.
issues.action: Reduce the header height and add a clear Executive Overview title, an as-of or last-refresh date, and a short dynamic scope subtitle. Place compact filters within the same structured header row.

issues.observed: A trial-version capacity warning is visible across the top of the deployed report.
issues.desired: A board-facing dashboard should be delivered without licensing, trial or administrative notices.
issues.action: Publish or embed the report through appropriately licensed production capacity so the trial warning is removed. This is a deployment and licensing correction rather than a report-theme adjustment.

issues.observed: RiskCount is shown as 14 in the same neutral styling as the other KPIs, without threshold, severity, trend, definition or navigation to the underlying risks.
issues.desired: The risk KPI should communicate whether the count is acceptable, worsening or urgent and should support investigation.
issues.action: Rename the label to Risk Areas, apply conditional status colour based on an approved threshold measure, show change versus the prior comparable period, and provide a tooltip or drill-through to the risk detail page.

issues.observed: Cards and chart titles expose model-style names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarginPct, YoYGrowthPct and RiskCount rather than executive-friendly language.
issues.desired: Titles should use natural business terminology and clarify units and comparison periods.
issues.action: Use display labels such as Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth and Risk Areas. Replace autogenerated chart titles with concise titles and subtitles that identify the period and comparison basis.

issues.observed: The KPI values are large enough to see, but they have no prior-period comparison, target variance, status indicator or supporting trend.
issues.desired: Board-level KPI cards should answer not only what the value is, but whether performance is improving and whether it is on plan.
issues.action: Add compact comparison text such as versus prior year or versus plan, using existing validated measures only. Where useful, add a small trend sparkline and conditional status accent without changing the primary measure semantics.

issues.observed: Fiscal years are encoded as green and red, colours that usually communicate positive and negative performance. This gives a categorical year series unintended status meaning.
issues.desired: Time-series comparison colours should be neutral and clearly distinguish current versus prior period, while red and green remain reserved for performance status.
issues.action: Use a strong brand colour for the current year and a lighter neutral or muted shade for the prior year. Reserve red, amber and green for threshold-based positive or negative signals.

issues.observed: The large revenue trend occupies most of the middle row while the margin trend and two comparison charts are compressed into the bottom row. Long titles, legends and small labels reduce usable plot area.
issues.desired: The four analytical charts should have balanced prominence and sufficient space for axes, labels and comparisons.
issues.action: Adopt a balanced two-by-two chart grid beneath the KPI row, reduce redundant autogenerated title text, and allocate consistent padding and plot heights. Preserve more width for category labels where needed.

issues.observed: Axis labels, legends and category names are small, and the margin chart relies on angled month labels. This is difficult to read in a boardroom or when the report is projected.
issues.desired: Core labels should remain legible at normal Power BI fit-to-page viewing and on presentation displays.
issues.action: Increase axis and legend text sizes, shorten titles, reduce unnecessary gridlines, and use correctly ordered abbreviated month labels so horizontal labels fit without rotation.

issues.observed: The cards read as plain white rectangles separated by heavy green bands and gaps, with limited grouping, status accents or refined spacing.
issues.desired: KPI cards should form a cohesive first-level summary with consistent padding, restrained borders and deliberate status accents.
issues.action: Use a neutral page background, subtle card borders or shadows, consistent internal padding and a restrained brand accent. Avoid large decorative green blocks that do not encode information.

summary: The page contains all required KPI and chart subjects, but it does not yet provide a credible executive overview. The most serious analytical defect is the nonchronological month ordering, followed by unreadable mixed-unit regional and category charts and ambiguous filter context. The layout is structurally aligned but lacks a purposeful header, executive comparisons, risk context and production-level polish. Most improvements are achievable with standard Power BI modelling, formatting and native visuals.
reference_rejected_ideas: Do not copy the reference's Power BI application chrome or left navigation rail into the report canvas; those elements belong to the hosting experience and do not improve analysis.

The reference's date filter appears to cover January through April 2024 while its trend charts show May 2023 through April 2024. That scope mismatch should not be reproduced unless the charts are explicitly labelled as rolling 12 months.

The reference category chart overlays revenue bars and percentage dots on separately interpreted horizontal scales. Reproducing that exact treatment may require a custom visual; an aligned native revenue-and-growth presentation is safer and easier to govern.
Exact pixel-level shadows, icons and ornamental card details should not take priority over chronological sorting, measure clarity, filter consistency or accessibility.
